## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** In the reported setup (a direct boot entry on `omarchy_linux.efi` after migration 1789325478), `--refresh` repoints the entry to `omarchy_linux-omarchy.efi`, keeps its `BootOrder` position and sets `reboot-required`. A second run makes no changes. The config load order matches limine-entry-tool 1.39.0 (`/etc/default/limine` wins), and the `omarchy_<kernel>.efi` naming matches limine-mkinitcpio-hook. Creating the new entry before deleting the old one keeps an Omarchy entry present at every step, and a failed create deletes nothing. The PR's test passes on this head (7 of 7).

Several edge cases can still leave direct boot on the old kernel while the migration records success. The first affects the same firmware class the upper-case handling targets.

### Firmware optional data hides the entry from `--refresh`

efibootmgr 18 prints a boot entry's optional data directly after the loader path, with no separator. `current_uki=${existing_entry##*\\}` (`bin/omarchy-setup-direct-boot:87-88`) then keeps that data as part of the file name:

```text
Boot0001* Omarchy  HD(1,GPT,...)/\EFI\LINUX\OMARCHY_LINUX.EFI0000424f

current_uki = OMARCHY_LINUX.EFI0000424f
${current_uki,,} == omarchy_*.efi  ->  false  ->  exit 0 (treated as a custom entry)
```

Public reports show firmware that upper-cases paths also appending `0000424f` to entries, including OS-created ones (rhboot/efibootmgr#225 on MSI boards, fwupd/fwupd#6101). In a sandboxed run with a stub modelling efibootmgr 18 output, the suffixed upper-case entry produced exit 0 and no EFI writes. The same entry without the suffix was repointed correctly.

**Impact:** On such firmware the migration exits successfully without a message and is marked applied, and the machine keeps booting the old kernel: the #12145 symptom.

**Suggested change:** Match the loader path case-insensitively as `\EFI\Linux\omarchy_*.efi` and ignore anything after `.efi`, for example `grep -oiE '\\EFI\\Linux\\omarchy_[^\\]*\.efi'`. Print a one-line notice when an Omarchy entry is left unchanged. Untested consideration: efibootmgr#225 reports some MSI boards ignoring entries without the suffix, so a recreated entry may need the old optional data carried over.

**Related, directory and ESP not checked:** the ownership check compares file names only. In the same stub model, an Omarchy entry pointing at `omarchy_linux.efi` in another directory, or on another disk's ESP, was recreated on the `/boot` ESP under `\EFI\Linux\`. The PR description says entries outside the Omarchy UKIs are left alone. Matching the full `\EFI\Linux\` path as above covers the directory case. Comparing the entry's `HD()` partition GUID with the `/boot` PARTUUID would cover the other-ESP case. Every Omarchy code path creates the standard path, so this mainly affects hand-made entries.

### The replacement entry is identified by label

Line 101 takes the first `Omarchy` entry other than the old one as the new entry. efibootmgr assigns the lowest free boot number, so an existing second Omarchy entry with a lower number is picked instead. Stub run with a second Omarchy entry `0003` (old kernel) already present:

```text
--create            -> Boot0004  \EFI\Linux\omarchy_linux-omarchy.efi
new_num             -> 0003      (the other pre-existing entry)
final BootOrder     -> 0003,0002,0003,0000   (0004 missing)
first boot option   -> omarchy_linux.efi
script output       -> "Pointing direct boot at omarchy_linux-omarchy.efi ..."   exit 0
```

**Impact:** With a duplicate entry (manual, reinstall, or an earlier refresh interrupted between create and delete), the refresh reports success while firmware keeps booting the old kernel. The `--create` exit status (line 100) is also not checked.

**Suggested change:** Record the `Boot####` numbers before `--create`, check its exit status, and require exactly one new number afterwards.

### EFI write failures still report success

The `--delete-bootnum` and `--bootorder` calls (lines 108 and 111) discard output and ignore exit status. efibootmgr 18 rejects the whole `--bootorder` list if any number in it has no `Boot####` variable. Stub runs:

| Starting `BootOrder` | Final `BootOrder` | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `0001` (Limine), `0002` (Omarchy), `0007` (no entry), `0000` | `0003,0001,0007,0000`, new entry ahead of Limine | 0 |
| Control without `0007` | `0001,0003,0000` | 0 |

**Impact:** A user who had Limine first ends up with direct boot first. `reboot-required` is still set and the migration is marked applied, so it is not retried.

**Suggested change:** Filter the saved order to numbers that exist after the delete, check the status of the delete and reorder calls, and warn or exit non-zero instead of reporting success.

### Refresh runs before the AMI and Apple firmware refusal

The `--refresh` branch exits (line 115) before `bios_vendor` is read (line 118). Interactive setup refuses American Megatrends and Apple firmware, and `manual/47-system-snapshots.md` says setup refuses to run on them. In the stub model with an American Megatrends vendor string, the migration created, deleted and reordered entries, while interactive setup on the same system exited 1 with no changes.

**Impact:** The migration changes EFI entries without a prompt on firmware the project flags as risky for custom entries. Such a machine already accepted one Omarchy entry, so the practical risk is not established.

**Suggested change:** Apply the vendor check to `--refresh` too (printing how to switch back to Limine), or state in the script and PR why refresh is exempt.

### Unquoted `BOOT_ORDER` values are ignored

Line 30 only extracts double-quoted `BOOT_ORDER` values. limine-entry-tool 1.39.0 (`ConfigReader.java`) also accepts unquoted values and strips quotes only when present. With `BOOT_ORDER=linux` in `/etc/default/limine`, Limine prefers `linux`, while setup and refresh fall back to the drop-in and pick `omarchy_linux-omarchy.efi`. This comes from source analysis and was not executed.

**Impact:** A user's kernel preference in Limine and the direct boot entry disagree, and the refresh repoints the entry against that preference.

**Suggested change:** Accept unquoted values the way `ConfigReader` does, or take the first kernel from `limine-entry-tool --tree` (already used by 1789325478) instead of re-implementing the matcher.

**Optional test improvement:** The test's `efibootmgr` stub never prints optional data, numbers new entries as highest plus one, and accepts unknown `--bootorder` numbers, so the first three findings pass the current test. Modelling efibootmgr 18's listing, lowest-free numbering and `--bootorder` validation would catch them. The test's failure on the previous script comes from that script ignoring `OMARCHY_DIRECT_BOOT_ROOT` and exiting at its UEFI check, not from UKI selection.

**Note:** Migration timestamp `1789592128` is older than migrations already on `quattro` (for example `1790282866`). The runner still executes it, but regenerating it on rebase keeps the order consistent with `agents/skills/migrations.md`.
